title: [28/09/2025] Percentage of electricity production sources across four countries 2003-2008
prompt: The charts show the sources of the electricity produced in 4 countries between 2003 and 2008. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The pie charts illustrate the proportions of electricity generated from three different sources, namely fossil fuel, hydro power, and nuclear power, in India, Sweden, Morocco, and Vietnam during the period from 2003 to 2008.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, Morocco relied almost entirely on hydro power for its electricity production, while India was heavily dependent on fossil fuels. Additionally, Sweden was the only country among the four to utilize nuclear power as a significant source of electricity.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding countries where hydro power dominated, Morocco generated an overwhelming 95% of its electricity from this source, with the remaining 5% coming from fossil fuel and no contribution from nuclear power. Similarly, Sweden also relied heavily on hydro power, which accounted for just over half of its electricity production, at 52%. However, Sweden notably utilized nuclear power for 44% of its electricity, while fossil fuels accounted for only 4%.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for countries relying more on fossil fuels, India generated 82% of its electricity from this source, with hydro power making up 14% and nuclear power contributing only 4%. Meanwhile, Vietnam showed a more balanced distribution between its two main sources, with fossil fuel accounting for 56% and hydro power for 44%, while nuclear power was not utilized at all during this period.
